claims.title: How do the two finite markings recover an integral lattice?
claims.hypotheses: Work at a prime p with the linked arithmetic and unitary data, integral reference lattice, and a positive level N relatively prime to p. The two placed lattices lie in the prescribed genus away from p and have the prescribed half-perfect integral form at p. A positive rational similitude acts on the rational form. The two local lattice descriptions and their stabilizers are supplied.
claims.statement: The intersection of the p-inverted and p-local lattices recovers the integral lattice. One rational similitude satisfies both finite level coset tests if and only if it induces a marked, polarisation-preserving order-linear isomorphism of the two integral lattices. The level congruence descends integrally because N is prime to p.
claims.review: Both localizations are distinguished inside the rational space. The reciprocal implications and the content of the integral alternating forms are checked, including the prime 2.

claims.title: When do two marked periods give the same complex point?
claims.hypotheses: For the standard unitary datum a=m=1, the chosen infinite place has positive index one. All distinguished embeddings equal the specified embedding and the complex order action has the prescribed signature. Fix a prime p and principal level N prime to p. A marked uniformising family and the finite and real dictionaries give the point-set result for N>0; the cited theorem provides the standard complex family's uniformisation for N≥3.
claims.statement: The complex points of the standard model at level N≥3 are in bijection with the disjoint union over the admissible rational form classes of the diagonal rational-similitude orbits of the two finite right cosets and a positive complex line. For placed periods equality corresponds precisely to a polarised order-linear isomorphism preserving the level marking and an invertible complex-linear change of period coordinates.
claims.review: The finite conditions and the positive line use one rational similitude, whose inverse transports the rational period. The inverse construction transports the placement and the period along the same inverse lattice isomorphism. The realisation of the integral genus and the geometric existence of period sheets are identified as inputs.
